summary.en: Crowned co-ruler by her father George III and sole monarch from 1184, Tamar presided over the height of medieval Georgia's power and culture. Her armies defeated Muslim coalitions at Shamkor and Basiani, and she helped found the Empire of Trebizond. The Georgian Orthodox Church venerates her as a saint.
summary.zh: 由父王格奥尔基三世立为共治者，1184年起独立执政，塔玛尔统治时期是中世纪格鲁吉亚国力与文化的巅峰。其军队在沙姆科尔和巴西亚尼击败穆斯林联军，她还扶助建立了特拉比松帝国。格鲁吉亚东正教会尊她为圣人。

summary.en: A Uriankhai commoner who became Genghis Khan’s foremost general, Subutai led the great raid around the Caspian to the Kalka, helped destroy the Jin dynasty, and planned the invasion of Rus’ and Hungary under Batu.
summary.zh: 速不台出身兀良哈平民，成为成吉思汗麾下最杰出的将领，曾率军绕里海远袭至迦勒迦河，参与灭金，并在拔都统帅下策划了征服罗斯和匈牙利的西征。

summary.zh: 成吉思汗第三子及指定继承人，窝阔台完成灭金，在哈拉和林修筑都城，建立驿站制度，并派兵进攻欧洲、伊朗和高丽，1241年去世。

summary.zh: 在格里奥史诗中，松迪亚塔幼年残疾，后崛起将曼丁人从索索统治下解放。他在基里纳击败苏曼古鲁，建立马里帝国。一个世纪后，伊本·赫勒敦以“马里·贾塔”之名记载了他。

label.zh: 生于曼丁（传统认为在尼亚尼）

summary.en: Born in the Balkh region, he migrated with his family ahead of the Mongol invasions and settled in Seljuk Konya. His meeting with the dervish Shams of Tabriz transformed him into an ecstatic poet; his Masnavi is a masterpiece of Persian literature, and his followers formed the Mevlevi order.
summary.zh: 生于巴尔赫一带，蒙古入侵前随家人西迁，定居塞尔柱王朝的科尼亚。与托钵僧大不里士的沙姆斯相遇使他成为一位狂喜的诗人；其《玛斯纳维》是波斯文学杰作，门徒形成了梅夫拉维教团。

summary.en: Sent west by his brother Möngke, Hulagu destroyed the Nizari Ismaili fortresses, sacked Baghdad and executed the last Abbasid caliph in 1258, and founded the Ilkhanate in Iran, though his advance into Syria was checked at Ain Jalut.

summary.en: Ruler of Mali at its greatest extent, Musa made a celebrated pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324–1325, displaying such wealth in Cairo that Arab writers recalled it for decades. He annexed Gao and Timbuktu and patronised mosques and scholars, establishing Timbuktu as a centre of learning.
summary.zh: 穆萨统治时马里疆域最为辽阔，1324–1325年赴麦加朝觐，在开罗显示的财富令阿拉伯作家数十年津津乐道。他兼并加奥和廷巴克图，资助清真寺与学者，使廷巴克图成为学术中心。

summary.en: A Berber jurist from Tangier, Ibn Battuta travelled for nearly thirty years through the Islamic world and beyond, from the Swahili coast to China. His Rihla, dictated in Fez, includes the only eyewitness description of the court of Mali under Mansa Sulayman (1352–1353).

summary.en: A peasant girl from Domrémy who said saints' voices had commanded her to save France, Joan persuaded the Dauphin Charles to let her join the relief of Orléans in 1429. summary.en: Born at Talwandi (now Nankana Sahib) in Punjab, Nanak taught devotion to one formless God, equality regardless of caste or creed, and honest work. After long journeys he settled at Kartarpur on the Ravi, where the first Sikh community formed; his hymns are the core of the Guru Granth Sahib.

summary.en: The longest-reigning Ottoman sultan (1520–1566), known to Ottomans as Kanuni, "the Lawgiver". He took Belgrade, Rhodes and Baghdad, crushed Hungary at Mohács and besieged Vienna, while his reign saw a flowering of law, architecture and letters.

summary.en: A Rajput princess of Merta married into the ruling house of Mewar, Mirabai devoted herself to Krishna against family expectations and composed passionate devotional songs in Rajasthani and Braj. Legends of persecution surround her, and she is said to have ended her days at Dwarka. Her bhajans are still widely sung.
summary.zh: 米拉巴伊是梅尔塔的拉杰普特公主，嫁入梅瓦尔王室，不顾家族期望专心敬奉黑天，用拉贾斯坦语和布拉吉语创作热烈的虔信歌曲。关于她遭受迫害的传说众多，据称她晚年在德瓦尔卡辞世。她的颂歌至今广为传唱。

summary.en: Heir of the Habsburg, Burgundian and Spanish dynasties, Charles ruled the Low Countries, Spain and its American empire, southern Italy and, as emperor from 1519, the Holy Roman Empire. He fought France, the Ottomans and the Protestant princes before abdicating in 1555–56 and retiring to Yuste.
summary.zh: 查理五世集哈布斯堡、勃艮第和西班牙王朝遗产于一身，统治尼德兰、西班牙及其美洲帝国、意大利南部，并自1519年起为神圣罗马帝国皇帝。他与法国、奥斯曼帝国及新教诸侯连年征战，1555—1556年退位后隐居尤斯特修道院。

Mother of the Neo-Confucian scholar Yi I (Yulgok), she was later idealised as a model mother, and since 2009 her portrait has appeared on the 50,000-won note.

summary.en: Daughter of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn, Elizabeth survived imprisonment under her half-sister Mary I to become queen in 1558. Her reign settled a Protestant church, saw the defeat of the Spanish Armada and a flowering of literature; she died unmarried, the last Tudor monarch.

summary.en: A ruthless and innovative warlord from Owari who seized Kyoto in 1568, deposed the last Ashikaga shogun in 1573 and subdued much of central Japan, before being forced to suicide by his vassal Akechi Mitsuhide at Honnō-ji.
summary.zh: 出身尾张、行事果决而富于革新的战国大名。1568年进入京都，1573年放逐末代足利将军，平定日本中部大部分地区，后在本能寺遭家臣明智光秀背叛而自尽。

summary.en: A young Kongolese noblewoman, Kimpa Vita declared herself possessed by Saint Anthony and preached an Africanised Catholicism, urging the reunification of the war-torn kingdom. Her followers reoccupied the ruined capital São Salvador before King Pedro IV had her burned as a heretic.
summary.zh: 刚果年轻贵族女子金帕·维塔宣称圣安东尼附身，宣讲本土化的天主教，呼吁饱受战乱的王国重新统一。她的追随者重新占据已成废墟的首都圣萨尔瓦多，后国王佩德罗四世以异端罪将她处以火刑。

label.zh: 生于基班古山附近（约略）
追随者重占圣萨尔瓦多（姆班扎刚果）

label.en: Burned at Evululu on Pedro IV’s orders

role.en: Shah of Iran; founder of the Afsharid dynasty

summary.en: A soldier of the Afshar tribe of Khorasan who drove the Afghans and Ottomans out of Iran, deposed the last Safavids and was crowned on the Mughan plain in 1736. He sacked Delhi in 1739, but his harsh rule ended when his own officers assassinated him.
summary.zh: 呼罗珊阿夫沙尔部落出身的军人，将阿富汗人和奥斯曼人逐出伊朗，废黜萨法维末代君主，1736年在穆甘草原加冕。1739年洗劫德里，但统治严酷，最终被自己的军官刺杀。

label.zh: 生于呼罗珊达斯特格尔德

summary.en: A warrior-sultan of the Middle Horde, Ablai led Kazakh resistance to the Dzungars, balanced Russia and Qing China after the Dzungar collapse, and was proclaimed khan of all three hordes at Turkistan in 1771.

summary.en: A German princess born in Stettin, Catherine married the future Peter III and seized the throne from him in a 1762 coup. A correspondent of Enlightenment thinkers, she expanded Russia through wars with the Ottomans, the annexation of Crimea and the partitions of Poland.
summary.zh: 叶卡捷琳娜是生于什切青的德意志公主，嫁给后来的彼得三世，并于1762年发动政变夺取皇位。她与启蒙思想家通信往来，并通过对奥斯曼帝国的战争、吞并克里米亚和瓜分波兰大大扩张了俄国版图。

summary.en: A Fulani scholar of the Qadiriyya order, Usman dan Fodio preached reform in Hausaland for thirty years before leading the jihad of 1804. He wrote over a hundred works in Arabic, Fulfulde and Hausa and left the administration of the new caliphate to his son Muhammad Bello and brother Abdullahi.
summary.zh: 奥斯曼·丹·福迪奥是卡迪里教团的富拉尼学者，在豪萨地区宣讲改革三十年后，于1804年领导圣战。他以阿拉伯语、富拉语和豪萨语写下百余部著作，将新哈里发国的治理交给儿子穆罕默德·贝洛和兄弟阿卜杜拉希。

label.zh: 生于戈比尔的马拉塔（约略）

summary.en: An Albanian officer sent against the French, Muhammad Ali seized power in Egypt, destroyed the Mamluk elite and built a conscript army, state monopolies and factories. His campaigns reached Arabia, Sudan and Syria, and his dynasty ruled Egypt until the monarchy was abolished in 1953.
summary.zh: 穆罕默德·阿里原为奉派抗击法军的阿尔巴尼亚军官，夺取埃及政权后消灭马穆鲁克精英，建立征兵制军队、国家专营和工厂。其征战远及阿拉伯半岛、苏丹和叙利亚，他的王朝统治埃及，直至1953年君主制被废除。

label.zh: 生于卡瓦拉（奥斯曼马其顿）

label.en: Lands with Ottoman forces against the French
label.zh: 随奥斯曼军登陆抗击法军

summary.en: A Corsican-born artillery officer, Napoleon rose through the Revolutionary wars, seized power in 1799 and crowned himself emperor in 1804. His armies dominated continental Europe until the disastrous Russian campaign of 1812; defeated at Leipzig and finally at Waterloo, he died in exile on Saint Helena.
summary.zh: 拿破仑生于科西嘉，以炮兵军官身份在大革命战争中崛起，1799年夺取政权，1804年加冕称帝。他的军队称雄欧陆，直至1812年远征俄国惨败；此后他在莱比锡战败，最终兵败滑铁卢，卒于流放地圣赫勒拿岛。

summary.en: Born in Bonn, Beethoven settled in Vienna in 1792 to study with Haydn and became the city's leading pianist-composer. Despite growing deafness, described in his Heiligenstadt Testament of 1802, he wrote nine symphonies, the Missa solemnis and late string quartets bridging the Classical and Romantic eras.
summary.zh: 贝多芬生于波恩，1792年移居维也纳师从海顿，成为该城首屈一指的钢琴家兼作曲家。尽管听力日益衰退（1802年的《海利根施塔特遗嘱》对此有所记述），他仍创作了九部交响曲、《庄严弥撒》和晚期弦乐四重奏，成为连接古典主义与浪漫主义的桥梁。

summary.en: Trained in the army of the Mthethwa paramount Dingiswayo, Shaka took over the small Zulu chiefdom in 1816 and, through age-regiments and new close-combat tactics, forged a powerful centralised kingdom. He was assassinated by his half-brothers Dingane and Mhlangana in 1828.
summary.zh: 恰卡曾在姆特特瓦首领丁吉斯瓦约麾下受训，1816年接掌弱小的祖鲁酋邦，凭借年龄兵团与新的近战战术建立起强大的中央集权王国。1828年被同父异母兄弟丁冈与姆兰加纳刺杀。

summary.en: A Maninka trader turned military leader, Samori built the Wassoulou state with a disciplined army armed with imported breech-loading and repeating rifles, plus copies made by his own smiths. He resisted French conquest for nearly two decades, relocating his whole state eastward, until his capture in 1898.

label.zh: 生于马尼扬巴拉杜古（约略）

summary.en: A low-ranking samurai from Tosa who left his domain to work for national reform. He founded a trading company in Nagasaki, brokered the Satsuma–Chōshū alliance in 1866 and proposed the peaceful return of power to the emperor, but was assassinated in Kyoto weeks later.

summary.en: King of Shewa from 1865 and emperor from 1889, Menelik expanded Ethiopia south and west to roughly its modern borders, founded Addis Ababa with Empress Taytu, and defeated Italy at Adwa. He introduced railways, telegraphs and modern schools.

summary.en: Daughter of a Javanese regent, Kartini was secluded at home from the age of 12 but corresponded in Dutch with European friends about colonial injustice, polygamy and women's education. polity.zh: 伊弗里基叶诸伊斯兰王朝；奥斯曼突尼斯

summary.en: Destroyed by Rome in 146 BCE, Carthage was refounded as a Roman colony under Caesar and Augustus and became the second city of the Latin West. It was the Vandal capital and a Byzantine stronghold until Hassan ibn al-Nuʿman razed it in 698; today it is a suburb of Tunis and a World Heritage site.
summary.zh: 迦太基于公元前146年被罗马摧毁，在凯撒与奥古斯都时期重建为罗马殖民市，成为拉丁西方第二大城。它曾是汪达尔王国都城和拜占庭要塞，698年被哈桑·伊本·努曼夷平；今为突尼斯市郊和世界遗产。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Carthage
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Archaeological Site of Carthage
Procopius, History of the Wars, Books III–IV
Britannica: Carthage

places.note: Wikidata’s end date (146 BCE) refers to Punic Carthage; this genealogy covers the Roman and later city.

polity.zh: 哈里发治下的埃及（正统、倭马亚、阿拔斯；图伦、伊赫什德）

polity.en: Egypt under the Muhammad Ali dynasty (British-occupied from 1882)
polity.zh: 穆罕默德·阿里王朝治下埃及（1882年起英国占领）

summary.en: Founded by Alexander the Great in 331 BCE, Alexandria was the Ptolemaic capital, home of the Library and Pharos, and a centre of Greek, Jewish and Christian thought. After the Arab conquest the capital moved inland to Fustat; the port revived under Muhammad Ali and became a cosmopolitan city.
summary.zh: 亚历山大城由亚历山大大帝于公元前331年建立，是托勒密王朝都城，拥有图书馆与灯塔，也是希腊、犹太和基督教思想的中心。阿拉伯征服后首都内迁至福斯塔特；穆罕默德·阿里时代港口复兴，成为国际化都市。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Alexandria
Britannica: Alexandria
Christopher Haas, Alexandria in Late Antiquity (1997)

polity.en: Caliphal Egypt (Rashidun, Umayyad, Abbasid; Tulunids, Ikhshidids)
polity.zh: 哈里发治下的埃及（正统、倭马亚、阿拔斯；图伦、伊赫什德）

polity.en: Egypt under the Muhammad Ali dynasty
polity.zh: 穆罕默德·阿里王朝治下埃及

summary.en: The Roman fortress of Babylon guarded the Nile crossing; the Arab conquerors built Fustat beside it in 641. The Fatimids founded al-Qahira to the north in 969, and the two merged into the capital of the Ayyubids and Mamluks, the largest city of the medieval Islamic world.
summary.zh: 罗马的巴比伦要塞扼守尼罗河渡口，641年阿拉伯征服者在其旁建福斯塔特。969年法蒂玛王朝在北面建卡希拉，两城逐渐合一，成为阿尤布王朝和马穆鲁克王朝的都城、中世纪伊斯兰世界最大的城市。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Cairo
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Cairo
André Raymond, Cairo: City of History (2000)
Michael Brett, The Fatimid Empire (2017)

places.note: Fustat was formally abandoned in 1168; it is treated here as the predecessor settlement of Cairo. The Fatimid court moved to Cairo only in 973. Under the Ottomans Cairo was the seat of the province (eyalet) of Egypt.

polity.en: Tuareg seasonal camp, then trading town
polity.zh: 图阿雷格人季节营地，后为商镇
图阿雷格（马格沙伦）统治

polity.en: Pashalik of Timbuktu (Moroccan, later autonomous Arma)
polity.zh: 廷巴克图帕夏国（摩洛哥，后为自治的阿尔马）
图库勒尔帝国与图阿雷格人

summary.en: According to the Tarikh al-Sudan, Timbuktu began around 1100 as a Tuareg camp near the Niger. Under Mali and Songhai it became a hub of trans-Saharan trade and Islamic learning, with the Djinguereber, Sankore and Sidi Yahia mosques and libraries of manuscripts that survive today.
summary.zh: 据《苏丹史》，廷巴克图约于1100年作为尼日尔河附近的图阿雷格营地而兴起。在马里和桑海治下，它成为跨撒哈拉贸易与伊斯兰学术中心，拥有津加雷贝尔、桑科尔、西迪·叶海亚清真寺及至今尚存的手稿图书馆。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Timbuktu
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Timbuktu
al-Sa'di, Tarikh al-Sudan (c. 1655), trans. J. O. Hunwick, Timbuktu and the Songhay Empire (2003)

places.note: Foundation date traditional; the post-1591 sequence of overlords is simplified.

polity.en: Tulama Oromo lands (annexed by Shewa in the 1870s–80s)
polity.zh: 图拉马奥罗莫人土地（1870–80年代并入绍阿）

polity.zh: 德尔格 / 埃塞俄比亚人民民主共和国
埃塞俄比亚联邦民主共和国

summary.en: “New Flower” was founded in 1886 by Empress Taytu and Menelik II beside hot springs at Finfinne, below the older royal seat of Entoto. It became the imperial capital, the seat of the OAU in 1963 and today of the African Union.
summary.zh: “新花”城于1886年由泰图皇后与孟尼利克二世在芬芬温泉旁、旧王都恩托托山下建立。它成为帝国首都，1963年成为非统组织所在地，今为非洲联盟总部所在地。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Addis Ababa
Bahru Zewde, A History of Modern Ethiopia, 1855–1991 (2nd ed., 2001)
Richard Pankhurst, History of Ethiopian Towns from the Mid-Nineteenth Century to 1935 (1985)

places.note: The start of the Finfinne entry (1800) is an approximation; the Oromo name is older.

polity.en: Kilwa Sultanate (restored, under Portuguese and Omani pressure)
polity.zh: 基尔瓦苏丹国（复国，受葡萄牙与阿曼挤压）
阿曼苏丹国 / 桑给巴尔苏丹国

summary.en: The island city-state of Kilwa dominated the Swahili coast’s gold trade in the 13th–15th centuries; Ibn Battuta called it one of the most beautiful cities in the world. Sacked by the Portuguese in 1505, it declined, and the modern district centre moved to the mainland at Kilwa Kivinje and Kilwa Masoko.
summary.zh: 岛上城邦基尔瓦在13–15世纪主导斯瓦希里海岸的黄金贸易，伊本·白图泰称之为世上最美的城市之一。1505年遭葡萄牙人洗劫后衰落，近代的行政中心迁至大陆上的基尔瓦基文杰和基尔瓦马索科。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Kilwa Kisiwani
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Ruins of Songo Mnara
H. Neville Chittick, Kilwa: An Islamic Trading City on the East African Coast (1974)

places.note: Early dates rest on the Kilwa Chronicle; the 18th-century sequence is simplified.

polity.zh: 阿沃里约鲁巴聚落（贝宁势力范围）
尼日利亚殖民地和保护国

summary.en: Called Eko by its Yoruba and Benin rulers, the lagoon port received its Portuguese name, after Lagos in the Algarve, in the 15th century. A slave-trading kingdom under Benin suzerainty, it was annexed by Britain in 1861 and served as Nigeria’s capital until Abuja replaced it in 1991.
summary.zh: 约鲁巴与贝宁统治者称之为“埃科”，这座潟湖港口在15世纪以葡萄牙阿尔加维的拉各斯得名。它曾是贝宁宗主下的奴隶贸易王国，1861年被英国吞并，并为尼日利亚首都，直至1991年被阿布贾取代。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Lagos
Kristin Mann, Slavery and the Birth of an African City: Lagos, 1760–1900 (2007)
Britannica: Lagos

places.note: The 1472 start follows Wikidata (Portuguese naming); the founding of the Lagos monarchy c. 1600 is approximate.

polity.en: French colony of Chad (French Equatorial Africa from 1910)
polity.zh: 法属乍得殖民地（1910年起属法属赤道非洲）

summary.en: Émile Gentil founded Fort-Lamy on 29 May 1900, naming it after Commandant Lamy, killed five weeks earlier at the Battle of Kousséri against Rabih az-Zubayr. President Tombalbaye renamed the capital in 1973 after the nearby Arab village of Niǧāmīnā.
summary.zh: 1900年5月29日，埃米尔·让蒂尔建立拉密堡，以五周前在与拉比赫·祖拜尔的库塞里之战中阵亡的拉密少校命名。1973年托姆巴巴耶总统以附近阿拉伯村落尼贾米纳之名为首都改名。

sources.title: Wikipedia: N'Djamena
Britannica: N’Djamena
Mario J. Azevedo & Emmanuel U. Nnadozie, Chad: A Nation in Search of Its Future (1998)

polity.zh: 刚果共和国（利奥波德维尔）；1964年起称刚果民主共和国
刚果民主共和国（1971–1997年为扎伊尔）

summary.en: Stanley set up a station below Boyoma (Stanley) Falls in 1883, where the Swahili-Arab trader Tippu Tip was briefly made governor in 1887. Stanleyville was Lumumba’s political stronghold and seat of rival governments in 1960–64, and was renamed Kisangani in 1966.
summary.zh: 1883年斯坦利在博约马（斯坦利）瀑布下设站，1887年斯瓦希里—阿拉伯商人蒂普·蒂普曾短暂任总督。斯坦利维尔是卢蒙巴的政治大本营，1960–64年间为对立政府所在地，1966年改名基桑加尼。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Kisangani

刚果民主共和国（1971–1997年为扎伊尔）

summary.en: Founded in 1910 as a copper-mining town and named after Queen Elisabeth of Belgium, Élisabethville was the headquarters of the Union Minière du Haut-Katanga. It was capital of Moïse Tshombe’s secessionist Katanga (1960–63) and was renamed Lubumbashi, after a local river, in 1966.
summary.zh: 伊丽莎白维尔建于1910年，为铜矿城镇，以比利时伊丽莎白王后命名，是上加丹加矿业联合公司总部所在地。1960–63年为冲伯领导的分离主义加丹加首都，1966年以当地河流之名改称卢本巴希。

polity.zh: 摩洛哥帕夏国，后属巴马纳塞古势力范围

summary.en: Excavations at Jenne-jeno, 3 km from the present town, revealed one of the oldest cities of sub-Saharan Africa, occupied from c. 250 BCE. Its successor Djenné became a Niger trading partner of Timbuktu, was taken by Sonni Ali after a long siege, and is famous for its mud-brick Great Mosque.
summary.zh: 距今城3公里的杰内-杰诺遗址发掘出撒哈拉以南最古老的城市之一，约公元前250年起有人居住。继起的杰内成为廷巴克图在尼日尔河上的贸易伙伴，经长期围城后被索尼·阿里攻占，以泥砖大清真寺闻名。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Djenné

places.note: The shift from Jenne-jeno to Djenné (c. 1100–1400) is dated archaeologically; the 1250 boundary is approximate.

polity.zh: 埃塞俄比亚帝国（王子纷争时代）

summary.en: Founded by Emperor Fasilides as the first fixed capital of the Solomonic monarchy, Gondar flourished with castles, churches and Ethiopia’s greatest painting tradition. During the Era of the Princes the emperors there became puppets of regional lords, and Tewodros II abandoned it in 1855.
summary.zh: 贡德尔由法西利达斯皇帝建立，是所罗门王朝第一个固定都城，以城堡、教堂和埃塞俄比亚最杰出的绘画传统而繁荣。在王子纷争时代，此地的皇帝沦为地方诸侯的傀儡，1855年特沃德罗斯二世弃之他迁。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Gondar
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Fasil Ghebbi, Gondar Region
Richard Pankhurst, The Ethiopians: A History (1998)

summary.en: Sogdian Marakanda, taken by Alexander, grew into the hub of Silk Road trade, was destroyed by Genghis Khan in 1220 and rebuilt by Timur as his imperial capital, whose Registan and mausolea are among the masterpieces of Islamic architecture.
summary.zh: 粟特的马拉坎达曾被亚历山大攻占，后发展为丝绸之路贸易的枢纽；1220年被成吉思汗摧毁，又被帖木儿重建为帝国都城，其雷吉斯坦广场和诸陵墓是伊斯兰建筑的杰作。

summary.en: Capital of the Samanids and a famed centre of Islamic learning—Ibn Sina studied in its library—Bukhara survived the Mongol sack to become seat of the Shaybanid khans and the emirs of Bukhara until the Red Army took it in 1920.
summary.zh: 布哈拉是萨曼王朝的都城和著名的伊斯兰学术中心（伊本·西那曾在其图书馆求学），经蒙古洗劫后复兴，成为昔班尼汗国和布哈拉埃米尔的都城，直至1920年被红军攻占。

summary.en: Founded as the Russian fort of Verny in 1854 below the Zailiysky Alatau, the town became Alma-Ata in 1921 and capital of Soviet Kazakhstan from 1929; it remained the capital of independent Kazakhstan until 1997 and is still its largest city.
summary.zh: 1854年俄国在外伊犁阿拉套山下建立维尔内要塞，1921年改名阿拉木图，1929年起为苏联哈萨克的首府；独立后的哈萨克斯坦以其为首都直至1997年，至今仍是该国最大城市。

summary.en: The oasis of Chach (Chinese Shi, “stone”) on the Chirchik became Tashkent (“stone city”) under the Karakhanids. Taken by Kokand and then by Russia in 1865, it served as capital of Russian Turkestan and is now Uzbekistan’s capital and Central Asia’s largest city.
summary.zh: 奇尔奇克河畔的赭时绿洲（汉文称“石国”）在喀喇汗时期称为塔什干（意为“石城”）。先后为浩罕和俄国（1865年）所占，曾为俄属突厥斯坦首府，今为乌兹别克斯坦首都和中亚最大城市。

summary.en: Successive walled cities in the Murghab oasis made Merv a capital of Khurasan, the launch-point of the Abbasid revolution in 747 and Sanjar’s Seljuk seat. Destroyed by the Mongols in 1221, its ruins lie beside the Russian-founded town of Mary.
summary.zh: 穆尔加布绿洲上相继兴建的城池使梅尔夫成为呼罗珊的首府、747年阿拔斯革命的发源地以及桑贾尔的塞尔柱都城。1221年遭蒙古摧毁，其遗址位于俄国人建立的马雷城旁。

summary.en: Genghis Khan chose the Orkhon valley site in 1220 and Ögedei walled it in 1235 as the imperial capital, visited by envoys such as William of Rubruck. After Ming troops destroyed it in 1388, the Erdene Zuu monastery rose from its stones in 1585.
summary.zh: 成吉思汗于1220年选定鄂尔浑河谷此地，窝阔台于1235年筑城定为帝国都城，鲁布鲁克等使节曾到访。1388年被明军摧毁后，1585年人们以其石料修建了额尔德尼召寺。

summary.en: A Cossack outpost founded in 1830 on the Ishim, Akmolinsk became Tselinograd, hub of the Virgin Lands campaign, in 1961. Renamed Akmola and then Astana (“capital”), it replaced Almaty as Kazakhstan’s capital in 1997; it was called Nur-Sultan from 2019 to 2022.
summary.zh: 1830年哥萨克在伊希姆河畔建立阿克莫林斯克要塞，1961年更名切利诺格勒，成为垦荒运动的中心。后改名阿克莫拉，再改为阿斯塔纳（意为“首都”），1997年取代阿拉木图成为哈萨克斯坦首都；2019年至2022年曾称努尔苏丹。

summary.en: The Kokand fortress of Pishpek in the Chu valley was destroyed by Russian troops in 1862 and replaced by a settler town. Renamed Frunze after the Bolshevik commander born there, it became capital of Soviet Kyrgyzstan and took the name Bishkek in 1991.
summary.zh: 楚河谷地的浩罕要塞皮什佩克于1862年被俄军摧毁，其旁兴起移民城镇。后以生于此地的布尔什维克将领伏龙芝之名命名，成为苏联吉尔吉斯的首府，1991年改名比什凯克。

polity.zh: 俄罗斯帝国 / 俄罗斯共和国 / 苏维埃俄国

summary.en: Founded by Peter the Great on the Neva delta in 1703, the city replaced Moscow as Russia's capital from 1712 to 1918. It was renamed Petrograd in 1914 to sound less German, Leningrad in 1924 after Lenin's death, and Saint Petersburg again by referendum in 1991.
summary.zh: 1703年彼得大帝在涅瓦河三角洲建城，1712至1918年间取代莫斯科成为俄国首都。1914年为去德语色彩改名彼得格勒，1924年列宁逝世后改名列宁格勒，1991年经公投恢复圣彼得堡之名。

sources.title: Britannica: Saint Petersburg
Lindsey Hughes, Russia in the Age of Peter the Great (1998)

places.note: The capital move is usually dated 1712 (some say 1713); the Soviet government moved to Moscow in March 1918.

summary.en: Built in 1589 as the fortress of Tsaritsyn guarding the lower Volga, the city was renamed Stalingrad in 1925 and became the scene of the decisive battle of 1942–43. During de-Stalinisation it was renamed Volgograd in 1961.
summary.zh: 该城始建于1589年，为扼守伏尔加河下游的察里津要塞，1925年改名斯大林格勒，1942—1943年成为决定性战役的战场。1961年去斯大林化期间改名伏尔加格勒。

sources.title: Britannica: Volgograd
Antony Beevor, Stalingrad (1998)

polity.zh: 波利安人（东斯拉夫部落）

polity.en: Rus' principality under the Golden Horde
polity.zh: 金帐汗国治下的罗斯公国
俄罗斯沙皇国（哥萨克酋长国）

polity.en: Contested: Ukrainian People's Republic / Soviet forces
polity.zh: 争夺中：乌克兰人民共和国 / 苏维埃军队
乌克兰苏维埃社会主义共和国（1922年起属苏联）
乌克兰苏维埃社会主义共和国（苏联）

summary.en: Capital of Kievan Rus' from the late 9th century, Kyiv was devastated by the Mongols in 1240 and later ruled by Lithuania, Poland–Lithuania and Russia. Capital of Soviet Ukraine from 1934, it became capital of independent Ukraine in 1991.
summary.zh: 基辅自9世纪末起为基辅罗斯首都，1240年遭蒙古人摧毁，此后先后由立陶宛、波兰—立陶宛和俄国统治。1934年起为苏维埃乌克兰首都，1991年成为独立的乌克兰首都。

sources.title: Britannica: Kyiv
Russian Primary Chronicle (legend of Kyi; Oleg's capture of Kyiv, 882)
Serhii Plokhy, The Gates of Europe: A History of Ukraine (2015)

places.note: The founding date 482 (Wikidata) is a traditional figure set for the city's 1500th anniversary in 1982; 882 for Oleg follows the Primary Chronicle. Kharkiv was capital of Soviet Ukraine until 1934.

polity.zh: 罗马帝国（诺里库姆 / 潘诺尼亚）

polity.en: Successive rulers: Lombards, Avars, Carolingian March
polity.zh: 相继统治者：伦巴第人、阿瓦尔人、加洛林边区
奥地利边区（神圣罗马帝国）
奥地利公国（巴本贝格家族）
哈布斯堡奥地利（神圣罗马帝国）

summary.en: The Roman legionary fortress of Vindobona on the Danube frontier grew into medieval Wien, seat of the Babenberg dukes from 1155 and of the Habsburgs from 1278. It was the capital of the Habsburg monarchy and Austria-Hungary, and of the Austrian republic except during the 1938–45 annexation.
summary.zh: 多瑙河边疆上的罗马军团要塞文多博纳发展为中世纪的维也纳，1155年起为巴本贝格公爵驻地，1278年起为哈布斯堡家族驻地。它是哈布斯堡君主国和奥匈帝国的首都，除1938—1945年被吞并期间外，也一直是奥地利共和国首都。

sources.title: Britannica: Vienna
Pieter M. Judson, The Habsburg Empire: A New History (2016)

places.note: The legionary fortress dates from c. 97 CE; the Roman period here starts with the annexation of Noricum (15 BCE). The name Wenia is first recorded in 881; 488 marks the Roman evacuation of Noricum.

image.file: Wien katedra sw Szczepana widok z wiezy 6.jpg

polity.zh: 罗马共和国 / 罗马帝国
罗马帝国（下日耳曼尼亚行省首府）

polity.en: Franks: Ripuarian kingdom, Francia, Lotharingia, East Francia
polity.zh: 法兰克人：里普利安王国、法兰克王国、洛林、东法兰克

polity.en: Holy Roman Empire (Electorate / Free Imperial City)
polity.zh: 神圣罗马帝国（选侯国 / 帝国自由城市）
法兰西共和国 / 法兰西第一帝国

summary.en: Founded as the Oppidum Ubiorum, a town of the Ubii resettled by Rome, it received colonial status in 50 CE, named after Agrippina, wife of Emperor Claudius. Taken by the Franks in the 5th century, it became a great archbishopric and trading city of the Holy Roman Empire, then passed to France and Prussia.
summary.zh: 该城始为罗马安置的乌比人城镇，公元50年获殖民地地位，并以克劳狄乌斯皇帝之妻阿格里皮娜命名。5世纪为法兰克人所占，后成为神圣罗马帝国重要的大主教驻地和商业城市，近代先后归属法国和普鲁士。

sources.title: Britannica: Cologne
Tacitus, Annals XII.27 (foundation of the colonia)

places.note: The Frankish takeover is dated c. 459; 38 BCE for the Ubii resettlement is traditional (dates between 38 and 19 BCE are proposed).

polity.zh: 罗马帝国（下不列颠尼亚行省首府）
德伊勒 / 诺森布里亚王国

summary.en: Founded as the legionary fortress of Eboracum in 71 CE, York was where Constantine the Great was proclaimed emperor in 306. It became Anglian Eoforwic, the Viking capital Jórvík after 866, and an archbishopric and leading city of medieval northern England.
summary.zh: 约克始建于公元71年，为罗马军团要塞埃博拉库姆，306年君士坦丁大帝在此被拥立为帝。此后它成为盎格鲁人的埃奥福维克，866年后为维京人的都城约维克，中世纪时是英格兰北部的大主教驻地和首要城市。

sources.title: Britannica: York
Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, entries for 866–867 and 954

polity.en: Byzantine Empire, contested by Huns, Avars and Slavs
polity.zh: 拜占庭帝国（为匈人、阿瓦尔人、斯拉夫人所争夺）
争夺中：拜占庭、匈牙利、保加利亚

polity.en: Kingdom of Syrmia (Serbian) / Kingdom of Hungary
polity.zh: 斯雷姆王国（塞尔维亚） / 匈牙利王国
革命塞尔维亚（第一次塞尔维亚起义）

polity.en: Ottoman Empire (autonomous Principality of Serbia from 1815–30, seat at Kragujevac)
polity.zh: 奥斯曼帝国（1815—1830年起塞尔维亚公国自治，驻地克拉古耶瓦茨）

polity.en: Principality of Serbia (Ottoman vassal until 1878) / Kingdom of Serbia (from 1882)
polity.zh: 塞尔维亚公国（1878年前为奥斯曼藩属）/ 塞尔维亚王国（1882年起）
南斯拉夫联盟共和国 / 塞尔维亚和黑山

summary.en: The Celtic and Roman Singidunum at the Sava–Danube confluence was fought over for centuries; its Slavic name, 'white city', first appears in 878. A Serbian capital in 1403–27, it was Hungarian and then Ottoman, became the capital of Serbia again in the 19th century and later of Yugoslavia.
summary.zh: 位于萨瓦河与多瑙河交汇处的辛吉杜努姆原为凯尔特和罗马城镇，数百年间屡遭争夺；其斯拉夫语名称意为“白城”，最早见于878年。1403至1427年为塞尔维亚首都，后归匈牙利和奥斯曼帝国，19世纪重新成为塞尔维亚首都，后又为南斯拉夫首都。

sources.title: Britannica: Belgrade
Letter of Pope John VIII to Boris I of Bulgaria (878), first mention of Beligrad

places.note: Many short-lived changes of rule (especially 6th–13th c.) are simplified. Belgrade was the seat of the rebel Governing Council in 1807–13 and Serbia’s princely capital from 1841, though an Ottoman garrison held the fortress until 1867. Wartime occupations (Austro-Hungarian 1915–18, German 1941–44) are not shown separately.

polity.en: State of the Teutonic Order (seat of the Grand Master from 1457)
polity.zh: 条顿骑士团国（1457年起为大团长驻地）
苏联（俄罗斯苏维埃联邦社会主义共和国）

summary.en: Founded by the Teutonic Knights in 1255 and named in honour of King Ottokar II of Bohemia, Königsberg became the capital of ducal Prussia and the coronation city of Prussian kings; Immanuel Kant lived there. Taken by the Red Army in 1945, it was annexed by the USSR and renamed Kaliningrad in 1946.
summary.zh: 柯尼斯堡由条顿骑士团于1255年建立，以纪念波希米亚国王奥托卡二世而得名，后成为普鲁士公国首都和普鲁士国王的加冕之城，哲学家康德即居于此。1945年被红军攻占，随后并入苏联，1946年改名加里宁格勒。

sources.title: Britannica: Kaliningrad
Christopher Clark, Iron Kingdom: The Rise and Downfall of Prussia (2006)

places.note: Renamed on 4 July 1946. The Duchy of Prussia was a Polish fief until 1657.

image.file: Old cathedral of Kaliningrad in Russia.jpg

polity.zh: 波兰 / 东波美拉尼亚公国

polity.en: Kingdom of Poland (Royal Prussia); Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth from 1569
polity.zh: 波兰王国（王室普鲁士）；1569年起属波兰—立陶宛联邦
但泽自由市（拿破仑时期）

polity.en: Free City of Danzig (League of Nations)

summary.en: First recorded in 997 as urbs Gyddanyzc in the Life of St Adalbert, the port was seized by the Teutonic Knights in 1308 and flourished as a Hanseatic city under the Polish crown after 1454. Prussian from 1793, a Free City between the world wars, it became Polish in 1945.
summary.zh: 该港最早于997年以“格但斯克城”之名见于《圣阿达尔贝特传》，1308年被条顿骑士团占领，1454年后在波兰王权下作为汉萨同盟城市而繁荣。1793年归普鲁士，两次世界大战之间为自由市，1945年归属波兰。

sources.title: Britannica: Gdańsk
Vita prima Sancti Adalberti (first mention, 997)

image.file: Calle Dlugie Pobrzeze, Gdansk, Polonia, 2013-05-20, DD 05.jpg

polity.en: Roman Republic / Roman Empire (capital of Macedonia)
polity.zh: 罗马共和国 / 罗马帝国（马其顿行省首府）
帖撒罗尼迦帝国（伊庇鲁斯系）
拜占庭帝国（尼西亚，后为君士坦丁堡）

summary.en: Founded by King Cassander of Macedon in 315 BCE and named after his wife, a half-sister of Alexander the Great, the city was the second city of the Byzantine Empire. Ottoman Selanik from 1430, it had a Sephardic Jewish majority for centuries before passing to Greece in 1912.
summary.zh: 该城由马其顿国王卡山德于公元前315年建立，以其妻（亚历山大大帝的同父异母姐妹）命名，曾是拜占庭帝国第二大城市。1430年起为奥斯曼帝国的萨洛尼卡，数百年间以塞法迪犹太人为多数居民，1912年归属希腊。

sources.title: Britannica: Thessaloníki
Mark Mazower, Salonica, City of Ghosts: Christians, Muslims and Jews, 1430–1950 (2004)

places.note: The first Ottoman rule (surrender in April 1387, returned to Byzantium by treaty with Süleyman Çelebi in 1403) is shown; the Norman sack of 1185 and the German occupation of 1941–44 are not shown separately.

image.artist: SilentResident (compilation, sources to attribute see above; if any of the sources used in the Montage are removed from

polity.zh: 罗马王政 / 罗马共和国
奥多亚克王国 / 东哥特王国

summary.en: By tradition founded in 753 BCE, Rome was the capital of the Roman Republic and Empire, though emperors increasingly resided elsewhere after the 3rd century. After Gothic and Byzantine rule it became the capital of the Papal States, and in 1871 the capital of united Italy.
summary.zh: 罗马相传建于公元前753年，是罗马共和国和罗马帝国的首都，但3世纪后皇帝日益常驻他处。经历哥特人和拜占庭统治后，它成为教皇国的首都，1871年成为统一后意大利的首都。

sources.title: Britannica: Rome
Livy, Ab Urbe Condita, Book I

places.note: 753 BCE is the traditional (Varronian) founding date. Rome was captured by the Kingdom of Italy in September 1870 and proclaimed capital in 1871; brief French-era interruptions (1798–99, 1809–14) are not shown.

polity.zh: 弗拉基米尔—苏兹达尔公国
俄罗斯沙皇国 / 俄罗斯帝国

summary.en: First mentioned in a chronicle under 1147, Moscow rose as the seat of a grand principality that gathered the Russian lands, and as the capital of the tsars. Peter the Great moved the capital to Saint Petersburg in 1712; the Bolsheviks restored Moscow as capital in 1918.
summary.zh: 莫斯科最早见于编年史1147年条目，后作为统一罗斯诸地的大公国驻地和沙皇首都而兴起。1712年彼得大帝迁都圣彼得堡，1918年布尔什维克政权重新定都莫斯科。

sources.title: Britannica: Moscow
Hypatian Chronicle, entry for 1147

image.file: Saint Basil's Cathedral and the Red Square.jpg

summary.en: A fishing village where Ōta Dōkan built Edo Castle in 1457, Edo became the seat of the Tokugawa shoguns in 1603 and one of the world's largest cities. Renamed Tokyo ("eastern capital") in 1868, it became the imperial capital.
summary.zh: 原为渔村，1457年太田道灌在此修筑江户城。1603年起成为德川将军的驻地，并发展为世界最大城市之一。1868年改称东京（“东方之京”），成为天皇所在的首都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Tokyo
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Marius B. Jansen, The Making of Modern Japan (Harvard University Press, 2000)
Wikipedia: Tokyo

summary.en: Founded by Emperor Kanmu in 794 as Heian-kyō on the model of Chang'an, Kyoto was the seat of the imperial court for over a thousand years and the centre of Japanese aristocratic and religious culture until the emperor moved to Tokyo.
summary.zh: 794年桓武天皇仿照长安建立平安京。此后一千多年里，京都一直是天皇朝廷所在地和日本贵族与宗教文化的中心，直至天皇移居东京。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kyoto
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto (Kyoto, Uji and Otsu Cities)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 2: Heian Japan (1999)
Wikipedia: Kyoto

image.file: Pedestrian road with pavements, paper umbrellas and people in yukata, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan.jpg

polity.zh: 朝鲜王朝 / 大韩帝国

summary.en: The Han River basin held Baekje's first capital and was fought over by the Three Kingdoms. Joseon made Hanseong its capital in 1394; under Japanese rule it was Keijō, and since 1945 it has been Seoul, capital of South Korea.
summary.zh: 汉江流域曾是百济最早的都城所在，并为三国反复争夺。1394年朝鲜王朝定都汉城；日本殖民时期称京城，1945年后称首尔（汉语旧称汉城），为韩国首都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Seoul
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Seoul

places.note: Early Baekje dates follow the traditional Samguk sagi chronology; the "Namgyeong" designation dates from 1067.

summary.en: Capital of Silla for nearly a thousand years, Seorabeol was renamed Gyeongju by Goryeo after Silla's surrender in 935. Its royal tombs, temples and observatory make it an open-air museum of Silla culture.
summary.zh: 徐罗伐作为新罗都城近千年，935年新罗归降后被高丽改名为庆州。城内王陵、寺院与瞻星台使其成为新罗文化的露天博物馆。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Gyeongju
Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Gyeongju Historic Areas
Wikipedia: Gyeongju

places.note: The 57 BCE founding date is traditional.

polity.zh: 唐安东都护府 / 边地
苏联民政局（苏联占领下的朝鲜北部）

polity.en: North Korea (Democratic People's Republic of Korea)
polity.zh: 朝鲜民主主义人民共和国

summary.en: Site of the Chinese Lelang commandery until 313, Pyongyang became Goguryeo's capital in 427. Goryeo made it the Western Capital, and since 1948 it has been the capital of North Korea.
summary.zh: 313年以前为中国乐浪郡治所，427年成为高句丽都城。高丽时期称西京，1948年起为朝鲜民主主义人民共和国首都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Pyongyang
Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Pyongyang

places.note: Lelang boundaries and dates before 313 are approximate. 1945–1948: seat of the Soviet Civil Administration and the Provisional People's Committee; the DPRK was proclaimed on 9 September 1948.

summary.en: Japan's first long-lasting capital, Heijō-kyō, was laid out here in 710. After the court left in 784, its great temples—Tōdai-ji, Kōfuku-ji, Kasuga shrine—kept Nara alive as the "southern capital" of Buddhism.
summary.zh: 日本第一座长期使用的都城平城京于710年在此兴建。784年朝廷迁离后，东大寺、兴福寺、春日大社等寺社使奈良作为佛教的“南都”延续繁荣。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Nara
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Monuments of Ancient Nara
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
Wikipedia: Nara (city)

summary.en: Wang Geon's home town of Songak became Gaegyeong, capital of Goryeo, for almost five centuries. Lying just south of the 38th parallel, it passed to North Korean control in the Korean War.
summary.zh: 王建的故乡松岳后来成为高丽都城开京，历时近五百年。开城位于三八线以南不远，在朝鲜战争中转归朝鲜控制。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kaesong
Goryeosa (History of Goryeo, 1451)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Monuments and Sites in Kaesong
Wikipedia: Kaesong

places.note: Taebong used Songak as capital only c. 898–905.

summary.en: As Naniwa it was a port and intermittent capital from the 7th century. Hideyoshi built Osaka Castle on the site of the Ishiyama Hongan-ji, and under the Tokugawa the city became Japan's commercial "kitchen".
summary.zh: 古称难波，自7世纪起即为港口，并几度成为都城。丰臣秀吉在石山本愿寺旧址修建大坂城；德川时代这里发展为日本的商业中心，号称“天下的厨房”。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Osaka
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Osaka

places.note: Naniwa served as capital only intermittently (645–655, 744–745); the 大坂→大阪 spelling change took place around 1868–1870.

summary.en: Minamoto no Yoritomo chose this coastal town, protected by hills, as his headquarters in 1180. It was Japan's political centre until the shogunate fell in 1333 and is known for the Great Buddha and Tsurugaoka Hachiman shrine.
summary.zh: 1180年源赖朝选择这座三面环山、一面临海的小城作为大本营。直到1333年幕府灭亡，这里一直是日本的政治中心，以镰仓大佛和鹤冈八幡宫闻名。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kamakura
Azuma kagami (Mirror of the East, late 13th c.)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 3: Medieval Japan (1990)
Wikipedia: Kamakura

polity.en: English Crown, then East India Company (from 1668)
polity.zh: 英国王室，1668年起东印度公司

summary.en: Seven islands ceded by Gujarat to Portugal in 1534 passed to England as part of Catherine of Braganza’s dowry in 1661. Reclaimed and joined, they grew into Bombay, India’s great port and financial capital, officially renamed Mumbai in 1995.
summary.zh: 这七个岛屿于1534年由古吉拉特割让给葡萄牙，1661年作为凯瑟琳公主的嫁妆转归英国。经填海连成一体后发展为孟买，成为印度最大的港口和金融中心，1995年正式更名为Mumbai。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Mumbai
Mariam Dossal, Theatre of Conflict, City of Hope: Mumbai 1660 to Present Times (2010)
Wikidata Q1156

image.file: Panoramic view of Taj Palace Hotel and Taj Tower with the iconic Gateway of India in the background (cropped).jpg

name.zh: 马德拉斯帕特南／马德拉斯（圣乔治堡）

summary.en: The East India Company acquired a coastal strip from a Vijayanagara nayaka in 1639 and built Fort St George, around which Madras grew as capital of the Madras Presidency. The city was renamed Chennai, after the neighbouring town of Chennapatnam, in 1996.
summary.zh: 东印度公司于1639年从毗奢耶那伽罗属下的纳亚克手中取得一段海岸并修建圣乔治堡，马德拉斯围绕该堡发展为马德拉斯管区首府。1996年依邻近的金奈帕特南之名改称金奈。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Chennai
S. Muthiah, Madras Rediscovered (2004)
Wikidata Q1352

name.zh: 加尔各答（卡利卡塔、苏塔努蒂、戈宾德布尔）

polity.en: East India Company (capital of British India)
polity.zh: 东印度公司（英属印度首府）

summary.en: Job Charnock’s East India Company post of 1690 on the Hooghly absorbed three villages and became Calcutta, capital of British India until 1911 and centre of the Bengal Renaissance. Its Bengali name Kolkata became official in 2001.
summary.zh: 1690年约伯·查诺克在胡格利河畔设立东印度公司商站，合并三个村落形成加尔各答；该城至1911年一直是英属印度首府，也是孟加拉文艺复兴的中心。2001年正式采用孟加拉语名称Kolkata。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kolkata
P. J. Marshall, Bengal: The British Bridgehead (1987)
Wikidata Q1348

polity.zh: 托马拉王朝与乔汉王朝

summary.en: Traditionally identified with the epic Indraprastha, Delhi has been rebuilt as a succession of cities: Tomara Dhillika, the sultanate capitals, Shah Jahan’s Shahjahanabad and Lutyens’s New Delhi, capital of British India from 1911 and of the Republic of India.
summary.zh: 德里传统上被认为即史诗中的因陀罗普拉斯塔，历史上曾多次重建为不同城市：托马拉王朝的迪利卡、苏丹国诸都城、沙贾汗的沙贾汉纳巴德以及勒琴斯设计的新德里；1911年起为英属印度首都，后为印度共和国首都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Delhi
Narayani Gupta, Delhi Between Two Empires 1803–1931 (1981)
Peter Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate: A Political and Military History (1999)
Wikidata Q1353

places.note: The Tomara founding (traditionally 736) is uncertain; Indraprastha is legendary and is not given a date range. Shahjahanabad was built 1639–1648.

polity.en: Pala Empire and later Bihar rulers
polity.zh: 波罗王朝及其后比哈尔诸政权
苏尔王朝，后为莫卧儿帝国
莫卧儿帝国／孟加拉纳瓦卜

polity.en: East India Company, then British Raj
polity.zh: 东印度公司，后为英属印度

summary.en: Pataliputra on the Ganges was the capital of the Maurya and Gupta empires and the city where Aryabhata worked. Lying in ruins by Xuanzang’s visit, it was refounded as Patna by Sher Shah Suri in 1541 and is now capital of Bihar.
summary.zh: 恒河畔的华氏城曾是孔雀王朝和笈多王朝的都城，阿耶波多亦在此著述。玄奘到访时已成废墟，1541年舍尔沙·苏尔在此重建巴特那，今为比哈尔邦首府。

sources.title: Upinder Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India (2008)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Patna
Wikidata Q80484

places.note: Polity labels before 320 and for 550–1541 are simplified; the Azimabad name (after prince Azim-us-Shan) was used alongside Patna.

polity.zh: 杜兰尼帝国／锡克米斯尔

polity.en: East India Company, then British Raj
polity.zh: 东印度公司，后为英属印度

summary.en: Capital of the later Ghaznavids, a Mughal imperial city adorned with the fort and Badshahi Mosque, and seat of Ranjit Singh’s Sikh Empire, Lahore became the capital of Punjab under the British and is Pakistan’s second-largest city.
summary.zh: 拉合尔曾是后期伽色尼王朝的都城、莫卧儿帝国的重要城市（建有拉合尔堡和巴德沙希清真寺），又为兰吉特·辛格锡克帝国的都城；英治时期为旁遮普首府，今为巴基斯坦第二大城市。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Lahore
Anna Suvorova, Lahore: Topophilia of Space and Place (2011)
Wikidata Q11739

image.file: Eye Of Lahore (Minar e Pakistan) evening.jpg

name.zh: 伊拉哈巴斯／阿拉哈巴德

summary.en: Prayaga, at the sacred confluence of the Ganges and Yamuna, hosted Harsha’s alms-giving assemblies and the Kumbh Mela. Akbar built a fort here and named it Ilahabas (1575), later Allahabad; the old name Prayagraj was restored in 2018.
summary.zh: 钵逻耶伽位于恒河与亚穆纳河的神圣交汇处，戒日王曾在此举行布施大会，也是大壶节举办地。阿克巴于1575年在此筑堡并命名为伊拉哈巴斯，后称阿拉哈巴德；2018年恢复古名普拉亚格拉杰。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Prayagraj
Abu'l-Fazl, Ain-i-Akbari (tr. H. S. Jarrett), Subah of Ilahabad
Wikidata Q162442

places.note: Akbar’s foundation is dated 1575 in most accounts, 1583 in some.

polity.en: Ghurids, then Delhi Sultanate and Jaunpur
polity.zh: 古尔王朝，后为德里苏丹国与焦恩布尔

summary.en: One of the world’s oldest continuously inhabited cities, Kashi on the Ganges is Hinduism’s holiest city and lies near Sarnath, where the Buddha first preached. Known to the British as Benares, it officially became Varanasi in 1956.
summary.zh: 迦尸位于恒河畔，是世界上最古老的持续有人居住的城市之一，也是印度教最神圣的城市，邻近佛陀初转法轮的鹿野苑。英国人称之为贝拿勒斯，1956年正式定名瓦拉纳西。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Varanasi
Diana L. Eck, Banaras: City of Light (1982)
Wikidata Q79980

places.note: Early polity labels omitted; date of the Benares State’s founding (1737) follows conventional accounts.

image.file: Varanasi, India, Varanasi skyline in the evening.jpg

summary.en: A harbour known to Arab traders (Ibn Battuta called it Kalanpu in 1344), Colombo was fortified by the Portuguese, made the Dutch and then British capital of Ceylon, and remains Sri Lanka’s commercial capital beside the administrative capital Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte.
summary.zh: 科伦坡早为阿拉伯商人所知（伊本·白图泰1344年称之为卡兰普），后由葡萄牙人筑城，相继成为荷兰与英国统治下锡兰的首府；今为斯里兰卡的商业首都，行政首都为毗邻的斯里贾亚瓦德纳普拉科特。

sources.title: K. M. de Silva, A History of Sri Lanka (1981)
Ibn Battuta, Rihla (tr. H. A. R. Gibb)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Colombo
Wikidata Q35381

places.note: The first name range starts at Ibn Battuta’s mention; the port is older. Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte became the official (legislative) capital in 1982; Colombo remains the executive and commercial capital.

polity.zh: 莫卧儿帝国（孟加拉省首府）

polity.en: East India Company, then British Raj
polity.zh: 东印度公司，后为英属印度
巴基斯坦（东巴基斯坦首府）

summary.en: Made the Mughal capital of Bengal by Islam Khan in 1610 and named Jahangirnagar after the emperor, Dhaka was famed for its muslin. It was capital of East Bengal and East Pakistan and, since 1971, of Bangladesh; the spelling Dhaka replaced Dacca in 1982.
summary.zh: 1610年伊斯兰汗将达卡定为莫卧儿孟加拉省首府，并以皇帝之名称为贾汉吉尔纳加尔，此地以细棉布闻名。后为东孟加拉和东巴基斯坦首府，1971年起为孟加拉国首都；1982年拼写由Dacca改为Dhaka。

sources.title: Richard M. Eaton, The Rise of Islam and the Bengal Frontier, 1204–1760 (1993)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Dhaka
Wikidata Q1354

places.note: Dhaka is first securely attested in a mosque inscription of 1459; Islam Khan’s move is dated 1608 or 1610 in different sources.

summary.en: A Khmer port called Prey Nokor, settled by Vietnamese in the 17th century and organised as Gia Định in 1698. As Saigon it was the capital of French Cochinchina and of South Vietnam, and was renamed after Hồ Chí Minh in 1976.
summary.zh: 原为高棉港口波雷诺哥，17世纪越南移民迁入，1698年设嘉定府。以西贡之名先后作为法属交趾支那和南越的首府，1976年以胡志明之名命名。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ho Chi Minh City
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: Ho Chi Minh City

places.note: The start of Vietnamese settlement and the date of the Khmer name are approximate.

polity.zh: 唐安南都护府 / 地方自主政权
阮朝 / 法属印度支那

summary.en: On the Red River, the Tang citadel of Đại La became Thăng Long when the Lý made it their capital in 1010. Renamed Hà Nội in 1831, it was the capital of French Indochina and has been Vietnam's capital since 1945.
summary.zh: 红河畔的唐代大罗城于1010年被李朝定为都城，改名升龙。1831年改称河内，曾为法属印度支那首府，1945年起为越南首都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Hanoi
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Central Sector of the Imperial Citadel of Thang Long – Hanoi
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Hanoi

places.note: Hanoi was also capital of French Indochina from 1902.

polity.zh: 荷兰东印度公司 / 荷属东印度

summary.en: The pepper port of Sunda Kelapa was taken by Fatahillah in 1527 and renamed Jayakarta. The Dutch rebuilt it as Batavia in 1619; renamed Jakarta during the Japanese occupation, it became the capital of independent Indonesia.
summary.zh: 胡椒港口巽他格拉巴于1527年被法塔希拉攻占并改名查雅加达。1619年荷兰人在此重建巴达维亚；日本占领期间改称雅加达，后成为独立的印度尼西亚首都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Jakarta
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 1: From Early Times to c. 1800 (1992)
Wikipedia: Jakarta

places.note: The start of Sunda Kelapa as a port is approximate; Wikidata dates the city's founding to 22 June 1527.

polity.zh: 孟族王国 / 东吁王朝

summary.en: A Mon town around the Shwedagon Pagoda, Dagon was renamed Yangon ("end of strife") by Alaungpaya in 1755. Under British rule Rangoon became the capital of Burma, which it remained until the government moved to Naypyidaw in 2005.
summary.zh: 大光原为瑞德宫大金塔周围的孟族城镇，1755年雍籍牙将其改名仰光（意为“战争终结”）。英国统治时期仰光成为缅甸首府，直至2005年政府迁往内比都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Yangon
G. E. Harvey, History of Burma (Longmans, 1925)
Victor Lieberman, Strange Parallels: Southeast Asia in Global Context, c. 800–1830, Vol. 1 (Cambridge University Press, 2003)
Wikipedia: Yangon

places.note: Wikidata's founding date of 1035 is traditional; 1000 is used as an approximate start.

summary.en: A riverside customs and fort town on the Chao Phraya under Ayutthaya, it became the capital when Taksin settled at Thonburi in 1767 and Rama I founded the new royal city on the east bank in 1782.
summary.zh: 阿瑜陀耶时期湄南河畔的关卡与要塞小镇。1767年郑信定都吞武里，1782年拉玛一世在东岸建立新王城，曼谷由此成为都城。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Bangkok
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
David K. Wyatt, Thailand: A Short History (Yale University Press, 2nd ed. 2003)
Wikipedia: Bangkok

places.note: The date of the early settlement is approximate.

image.file: Temple of the Emerald of buddha or Wat Phra Kaew (cropped).jpg

polity.zh: 菲律宾（法定首都为奎松城）

summary.en: A fortified Muslim trading settlement on Manila Bay, Maynila was taken by Legazpi, who founded the Spanish city in 1571. It was the hub of the trans-Pacific galleon trade and has been the Philippine capital except in 1948–1976, when Quezon City held the title.
summary.zh: 马尼拉湾畔设防的穆斯林贸易聚落，被黎牙实比攻取后于1571年建立西班牙城市。这里是跨太平洋大帆船贸易的枢纽，除1948—1976年奎松城为法定首都外，一直是菲律宾首都。

sources.title: Emma H. Blair & James A. Robertson (eds.), The Philippine Islands, 1493–1898, Vol. 3 (1903)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 1: From Early Times to c. 1800 (1992)
Wikipedia: Manila
Philippine News Agency/PTV: How QC became biggest LGU in Metro Manila (RA 333 of 1948; PD 940 of 1976)

places.note: The pre-Hispanic polity's origins are not precisely dated. Republic Act 333 (1948) made Quezon City the capital; Presidential Decree 940 (1976) restored Manila.

polity.zh: 马来亚联合邦；1963年起为马来西亚

summary.en: Founded by Parameswara around 1400, Malacca controlled the strait that bears its name and was the region's richest port. It passed to the Portuguese (1511), Dutch (1641) and British (1824), leaving a layered colonial townscape.
summary.zh: 马六甲约于1400年由拜里米苏拉建立，控制着以其命名的海峡，是区域最富庶的港口。此后相继归属葡萄牙（1511年）、荷兰（1641年）与英国（1824年），留下层叠的殖民城市风貌。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Melaka and George Town, Historic Cities of the Straits of Malacca
Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Wikipedia: Malacca City

places.note: British occupation 1795–1818 during the Napoleonic Wars is merged into the Dutch period.

summary.en: Named after the hill temple founded, by legend, by Lady Penh in 1372, the site at the confluence of the Mekong and Tonlé Sap became the Khmer capital after Angkor's abandonment and again under King Norodom in 1865.
summary.zh: 其名源于传说中奔夫人于1372年在山丘上建造的寺庙。此地位于湄公河与洞里萨河交汇处，吴哥被放弃后成为高棉都城，1865年诺罗敦国王再度定都于此。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Phnom Penh
David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Wikipedia: Phnom Penh

places.note: The 1372 founding and Ponhea Yat's capital dates are traditional.

summary.en: Yasovarman I founded Yasodharapura around 889, and for five centuries the Angkor region was the heart of the Khmer Empire. After 1431 the court moved south, though Angkor Wat remained a pilgrimage centre; Siam returned the province to French Cambodia in 1907.
summary.zh: 耶输跋摩一世约于889年建立耶输陀罗补罗，此后五个世纪里吴哥地区一直是高棉帝国的中心。1431年后王廷南迁，吴哥窟仍为朝圣之地；1907年暹罗将该省归还法属柬埔寨。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Angkor (Siem Reap)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Angkor
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Wikipedia: Angkor

places.note: The capital moved between Angkor and nearby sites (e.g. Koh Ker, 928–944).

summary.en: Capital of the first Burmese empire, whose rulers and subjects built over 10,000 Buddhist temples and stupas on the plain beside the Irrawaddy between the 11th and 13th centuries; more than 2,000 survive.
summary.zh: 缅甸第一个帝国的都城。11至13世纪间，君主与臣民在伊洛瓦底江畔的平原上建造了一万多座佛寺与佛塔，现存两千余座。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Bagan
Michael Aung-Thwin, Pagan: The Origins of Modern Burma (University of Hawaii Press, 1985)
Wikipedia: Bagan

places.note: The 849 founding date is traditional (chronicles).
